hook: Mehrotra built Allstate's entire AI Center of Excellence from the ground up, an 80-plus person team and a multi-year generative AI strategy, and now applies that same enterprise-AI playbook as Chief AI Officer at U.S. Bank.
name: Prashant Mehrotra

quote.text: Created and executing a multi-year AI strategy for Allstate that takes advantage of new Generative AI innovation to establish a market leading position for Allstate in the Insurance sector.
quote.context: Prashant Mehrotra, personal LinkedIn profile summary

moniker: Chief AI Officer at U.S. Bank

reading.body:
Prashant Mehrotra's career illustrates what enterprise AI deployment actually requires: years of infrastructure work, regulatory compliance, and data engineering before generative AI can produce measurable financial returns.

He spent six years at Allstate building the conditions for that outcome. The AI Center of Excellence grew to more than 80 people, and the platform it produced handled petabytes of voice, image, and document data while meeting privacy, security, and regulatory requirements. The multi-million-dollar annual cost savings the data attributes to that effort came after the infrastructure was in place, not before. His earlier work at Capital One, migrating card-division analytics to cloud systems across seven merchant integrations, follows the same sequence: data infrastructure first, capability second.

The pattern across his timeline is not one of sudden adoption but of compounding institutional investment. A 2002 start in data warehousing, a 2015 move to cloud migration, a 2018 pivot to AI platform construction, and a 2024 appointment as Chief AI Officer at a major national bank represents roughly two decades of layered technical work. What the data does not cover is the specific compute or power infrastructure underlying any of these deployments, the scale of U.S. Bank's AI operations, or what generative AI strategy he is now executing there.
